$comment: #EXP-1778: a Text `truncate: "middle"` line (start…end), HAND-AUTHORED and replayed by packages/exponential-ui/src/text-truncate.test.ts (`middleTruncateWidth`, the TS reference the web renderers measure with), apps/desktop/crates/eui-core/tests/text_truncate.rs (`middle_truncate_width`; gpui paints its own `text_ellipsis_middle`, the same rule) and the Swift + Compose renderers' tests. The rule = gpui's `TruncateMiddle`: per-character widths are SUMMED (no kerning across the cut); a line whose total fits `width` shows whole; else `budget` = `width` − the affix `…`'s width; `budget` ≤ 0 shows the `…` alone; else the longest START whose width ≤ budget × 2/3, the `…`, the longest END whose width ≤ the rest; the two meeting shows the `…` alone. #EXP-1789: a cut keeping FEWER THAN 4 characters (start + end together, `minKept`) shows the `…` alone too, so a nearly-gone run never reads as stray glyphs (`/h…/`); every renderer, the IDE's own path rows included, cuts by this rule rather than a platform ellipsis. Characters are user-perceived code points (an astral emoji is one). A case's `widths` = `default` per character plus `chars` overrides (the `…` included). `truncate: "end"` is the existing one-line ellipsis (Text `lines: 1`); both keep ONE line whatever `lines` says.

cases.name: one over: start two thirds, end one third
fractional budgets round down to whole characters
no room past the affix: the affix alone
narrower than the affix: the affix alone
a start too wide for its two thirds keeps none
mixed widths keeping three: the affix alone
three kept characters: the affix alone
a webhook URL keeps its host and its hook
